scope: CPU fake gallery and headless browser measurements only; no GPU, weights, real gallery, network performance or real phone acceptance.

checkout.head: 1b9138c4a3e83739ceadb27a25ddc97017639f56
checkout.provenance_note: Measured the local working tree during the overnight batch. Hashes describe the relevant sources when this receipt was written; this was not an immutable committed-tree benchmark.

fixture.construction: 5,000 separate storage.save_image calls on normalized requests, unique seeds and generated flat RGB pictures; separate temporary database and outputs. The fake adds two other-model rows, excluded by the normal selected-model gallery filter.

procedure: Open the isolated fake with the standard browser harness at 1400x900. Keep ordinary gallery pagination, lazy image loading and all card containment unchanged.
Time resetGallery through one animation frame: exactly 48 initial cards. Call the real loadGallery until all 5,000 selected-model records and cards exist, with exact count assertions.
Record long tasks and 30 large jumps spanning the entire gallery height. These jumps leave lazy thumbnails pending and measure DOM/layout stress, rather than settled image scrolling.

In a second fresh browser session, load all 5,000 cards, move to the tail and wait for visible thumbnails to decode. Wait again at the start of a nearby 1,200px range, then sample 30 requestAnimationFrame intervals while moving 40px per frame. Assert 5,000 cards and decoded visible thumbnails; inspect the final screenshot.

append_all_phase.large_jump_note: Pending lazy thumbnails after large jumps; not the settled-scroll result.

containment.conclusion: The append-every-card and large-jump stress paths have long tasks, while the first page and nearby scrolling with decoded thumbnails remain fast in this fixture. This does not establish a card containment benefit; no containment change was made.
